bytes: $0A00-$0AB3 (bits listed under 'unreferenced' in coverage.md section 4.9, plus D3 $019E-$01FF)
claim: No bit of coverage.md section 4.9 (261 bits: D2 28, D4 194, D5 27 non-scene ids, D6 $0400 and $04F7, D7 $0506-$0507, byte $0AA1 and $0508-$050F) and no D3 bit of $019E-$01FF is ever written during play. The static proof is S1-S9 of coverage.md (no literal COP, no gate operand, no helper candidate, no direct access to the byte except the bits named there); only a write census can catch a store through an address the scanner cannot resolve (MVN block copies, save/load, dynamic indexing).

trial.control: write-callback census over $0A00-$0AB3 with a positive control: take the natural first chest or the scene $0A letter and expect exactly one write at the ROM offset of the known setter (flag $3F at ec0A_left_guard.asm:32 {311322})
trial.forced: run the census along the natural route of FR10 and along each preset replay of FR50; save and load once
observe: PC of every write to a bit of the listed ranges, mapped to a ROM offset

confirms: no write to any listed bit except the save/load block copy of the whole array
refutes: a write with a PC outside the 1,693 literal sites and the 57 helper call sites to a listed bit: the bit is used by code the scanner missed

claim: Hazard for presets and census harnesses: ApplyAllEventBlocks scans all 256 D3 bits (event_blocks.asm:81 {172529}) but event_block_table.asm has 158 rows ($00-$9D); LookupEventBlock has no bound check, so a set bit in $019E-$01FF reads 8 bytes past the table (ROM offset 119758 + 8 * 158 = 121022 and up) and applies a block when the junk scene byte equals sceneCurrent. No code sets those bits, so the claim is that a harness write of $019E ($0A33 bit 6) is the only way to reach it.

trial.control: positive control: set $0106 (byte $0A20 bit 6), reload scene $0B and expect the prison-cell tiles to change (event block $06)
trial.forced: clear $0106, set $019E (byte $0A33 bit 6), reload scene $0B; then repeat with $0A20-$0A3F all 0xFF in a scene whose id equals the first byte of the 8 junk bytes at offset 121022
observe: map RAM and tile VRAM diff after the reload

confirms: the reload with $019E set copies no tiles in a scene that differs from the junk scene byte; the junk byte is read
refutes: the table is padded or the lookup stops at row 158

claim: TestFlag_0300(sceneCurrent) is called for every scene id (StandardEnemyDefeatHandler.asm:89 {56311}, :204 {56727}, radar_map_screen.asm:175 {229828}); for a tier-0 scene it reads a bit that nothing sets and the reward path ends without paying (tier 0). Scene $1B is such a scene (tier 0, has enemy-spawn rows): defeating its last enemy tests $031B and takes the no-reward branch without setting it.

trial.control: defeat the last enemy of a tier-1 scene (for example $0C) and expect $0300+scene to be set at 57679 or 50035
trial.forced: defeat the last enemy of scene $1B and read $0A63 bit 3 before and after
observe: breakpoint on TestFlag_0300 at ROM offset 56311 (carry result)
